summary: Friedrich Weller was an Indologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under August Conrady at the University of Leipzig (Dr. phil. ca. 1915, Habilitation ca. 1922), where he taught from ca. 1922 to 1958.

An Indologist and Tibetologist, Friedrich Wilhelm studied under Paul Thieme and completed his doctorate at the University of Munich (ca. 1951–1956). He held posts at Munich as Privatdozent (1963) and Professor (1969–1998).
Friedrich Wilhelm Graf is a scholar of religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Augsburg from ca. 1986 to 1999 and at the University of Munich from ca. 1999 to 2014.

Philosopher Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling studied at the Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Berlin (1841–1845).
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz (ca. 1889–1893) and Karl Foy.

Linguist Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg (Dr. phil. 1829). He held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (ca. 1829–1833), Breslau (1834), Bonn (1839), and Leipzig (ca. 1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and others, and completed a doctorate in theology at Munich (ca. 1836), where he held an extraordinary professorship (1838–1839).

Friedrich Zarncke was a linguist who studied at Rostock and Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Rostock (ca. 1847–1848) and Leipzig, where he was Privatdozent (1852) and Rektor (1869–1882).

Friedrich von Adelung worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology after studying at Leipzig (1787–1790). He held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809) and was director at Vienna (1824).

Friedrich von Spiegel specialized in Iranian and Indological studies. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Leipzig under Lassen, Brockhaus, and others, earning his doctorate at Jena (ca. 1842). He was professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1849–1891).

Frits Staal was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University, later holding professorships at Amsterdam (1962–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Philosopher Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen studied and habilitated at the University of Munich (1919–1928). He held professorships at Bonn (1934), Munich (1936–1941), and the University of Mainz (ca. 1947–1969).

Linguist and Indologist Frédéric Baudry studied under Eugène Burnouf (ca. 1845–1852). He worked as a librarian at Versailles (1849) and Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1859), and served as administrator of the Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885).
Fu Yan was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at the Royal Naval College (ca. 1877–1879). He held positions at Fudan University (ca. 1905–1906) and Peking University (ca. 1912).

Fu-shih Lin was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser (ca. 1988–1994), later working at Academia Sinica (ca. 1994–2021).

Fuguan Xu was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and history. He studied at Meiji University (ca. 1928–1931) and under Shili Xiong (ca. 1943–1950), later holding a post at Tunghai University (ca. 1955–1969).
Fujio Oda is an archaeologist and historian who studied at Kyushu University (ca. 1952–1956). He held academic posts at Beppu University (ca. 1968–1978) and Fukuoka University (ca. 1978–2004).

Fujio Taniguchi works in Buddhist, Indological, and Tibetan studies. He earned a PhD from Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa and others, and held an affiliation with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute attested in 2026.

Fumi Yao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Tokyo in 2011 and holds posts at the University of Tokyo and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2026.
